name: CLARIVATE PLC

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: This is the strongest version and I could not defeat it: at any defensible discount rate the market is requiring Clarivate's free cash flow to DECLINE, and the company is delivering flat. On the corrected 2026 run-rate base of roughly $520M of FCFF, the growth the market requires is +1.7% at a 12% WACC, -3.4% at 10% and -9.4% at 8%. Organic revenue is -0.4% and adjusted EBITDA is -1.3%, i.e. approximately flat. If flat is the right forecast, the equity is worth well above $1.84 at any WACC below about 11.5%. And the new tender offer is direct evidence that the 15.61% WACC is wrong: a company whose SECURED notes clear at 97.5 cents is not priced for distress by the people who actually lend to it.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: The 2028 maturity. Clarivate has to refinance the 3.875% notes, and the coupon it pays is the market's own answer to the cost-of-debt question this model gets wrong - it settles the WACC directly rather than by inference. Short of that, four consecutive quarters of positive organic revenue growth would convert 'flat' from a hope into a trend, and continued sub-par debt repurchases would keep transferring value to the equity.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Substantially yes, which is why the counter is strong. Organic ACV +1.5%, organic recurring revenue +0.7%, adjusted net income per share UP to $0.38 from $0.32 in H1, $122.9M of H1 free cash flow, and secured notes clearing at 97.5 - all visible today. What is NOT visible is total organic revenue turning positive: it is still -0.4%, held back by transactional revenue, and the headline revenue decline is amplified by divestitures.
devils_advocate.unresolved: The discount rate, and it decides the name. I can show the engine's 15.61% is wrong - actual interest expense over total debt is 6.81%, and the September tender cleared at 97.5 cents - but I cannot show what the right number is, and between 8% and 12% the equity is worth $6.29 and $1.27 against a $1.84 price. I also could not assess the AI substitution risk to Web of Science with anything better than judgement, and that is the variable the bear case turns on. Nothing in this pass changes the conclusion that the model output is unusable; what changed is that I can now name the defect precisely and cite a market price against it.

what_changed: Since this name was last recorded on 2026-09-18 at $1.90, one genuinely new event, and it is informative about the defect that dominates this name. Clarivate ran a cash tender offer for its 3.875% Senior Secured Notes due 2028, capped at $75M: announced 2026-09-17, priced 2026-09-23 at Total Consideration of $975.15 per $1,000, final results 2026-09-24. Those are the three 8-Ks in the last five sessions that helped win the opportunistic slot, and they are one transaction. The company is retiring secured debt at 97.5 cents on the dollar. Q2 2026 (2026-07-29): revenue $587.3M against $621.4M, organic revenue -1.5% with organic subscription +0.7% and organic ACV +1.5%; net loss $268.6M including the $221.7M impairment; adjusted net income $123.1M ($0.19); adjusted EBITDA $247.2M against $261.6M. H1: revenue $1,172.8M, organic -0.4%, adjusted EBITDA $488.4M, adjusted net income $242.4M (up 11%), operating cash flow $233.4M and free cash flow $122.9M.
consensus_case: At $1.84 the equity is $1.18B against $4.07B of net debt, so it is 22% of a $5.25B enterprise - a thin residual claim, and that is the whole story. The market is pricing a business whose organic revenue is flat at best (-0.4% in H1 2026, -1.5% organic in Q2), whose adjusted EBITDA is flat ($488.4M H1 against $494.8M), which just took a $221.7M non-cash goodwill impairment, and which carries $7.86B of purchase-accounting intangibles amortising through a reported EBIT of $71.5M. Leverage near 4x on an information-services asset facing generative-AI substitution in academic and IP research means small changes in enterprise value swing the equity violently, and the equity holder is paid last. A 22% free-cash-flow yield on the equity is what that risk costs.
base_case_rationale: I will not supply a growth rate for this name for the second time, and the reason is arithmetic rather than reticence. At a flat FCFF assumption the equity is worth $1.27 a share at a 12% WACC, $3.16 at 10% and $6.29 at 8% - the discount rate alone moves the answer from 31% below the price to 242% above it, because the equity is a levered sliver of the enterprise. There is no field in this schema that sets the WACC, and the WACC the engine used (15.61%, on a 79% debt weight) is the one input I can show to be wrong. Recording a fair value here would publish a number whose sign is set by an input I cannot correct; the prior pass recorded $0.04 a share, which is that failure made visible.
key_risks: The equity is 22% of enterprise value at ~4x leverage; the answer is a levered function of a discount rate nobody can pin to better than 4 points
Generative AI substitution in academic discovery and IP search against 0.7% organic subscription growth
$7.86B of intangibles amortising, with a $221.7M goodwill impairment already taken in Q2 2026
The 2028 secured maturity has to be refinanced and the current 3.875% coupon is almost certainly not repeatable
watch_for: The coupon on any refinancing of the 3.875% 2028 notes - the market's direct answer to this name's cost of debt
Total organic revenue growth turning positive; organic ACV is already +1.5% and recurring +0.7%
Further sub-par debt repurchases beyond the $75M tendered at 97.5
Adjusted EBITDA holding near the ~$1.0B annual run rate
